dr_brief.avatar: American woman 40-60, hospital nurse on 3x12s, mom, years of heel/arch pain after shifts
dr_brief.angle_habit: wearing running shoes she bought for comfort to 12-hour shifts
dr_brief.dream: nurse with energy left to cook for her kids after a 12
dr_brief.identification: limping to her car after a 12; shoes felt fine at 7 AM
dr_brief.point_of_contact: her shoes / the hard hospital floors (running nurse ads blame both: WA_NOT_NUR, Orthora 'by hour 6')
dr_brief.problem_mechanism: Her 'comfortable' sneakers were built for short forward runs: tapered toe box pinches, raised heel tips weight onto the balls of the feet, soft foam compresses by hour 4-6, and feet swell through the day so a 7 AM fit clamps by 2 PM.
dr_brief.function_mechanism: Insoles help others but she's on hard tile 12 hours and her feet swell: an insole eats the toe room in a shoe that's already tapered. She needs support that doesn't go flat, room that gives as feet swell, and a sole that rolls the step forward, all at once. Insoles sit in the same narrow shoe; clogs/orthotics don't give; memory-foam slip-ons collapse.
dr_brief.solution_mechanism: Ortho Stretch puts all three in one shoe: built-in arch support + cushioned rocker sole, stretch-knit upper + wide toe box that gives as feet swell, no-tie laces.
dr_brief.conditions: Her DIY fixes: sizing up (heel slips), insoles (eat toe room), clogs (no give). Sizing up slips at the heel; insoles eat toe room; most comfort shoes pick support OR give.
dr_brief.usp: support + room + roll in one shoe, at $59.95
dr_brief.anchoring: $59.95 vs the next $160 running shoes or insoles every few months; at 60% off less than a dollar a shift
dr_brief.risk_reversal: 30 days = 10+ shifts on her own feet; never 'easy returns'
